q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) NUM FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING NUM >= 5 ) AS A
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT CLASS, COUNT(DISTINCT STUDENT) NUM FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING NUM >= 5 ) AS A
explanation: Both queries aim to find classes that have at least 5 students enrolled. Q1 directly groups by CLASS and checks the count of rows (i.e., students) in each class. Q2 first groups by CLASS and counts the distinct students in each class, then filters for classes with at least 5 distinct students. Since both queries are essentially checking for classes with at least 5 students, they are semantically equivalent.
